conn.lost: the connection to the daemon dropped: {error}
daemon.already_running: a daemon is already running on this socket: {sock}
daemon.gone: daemon process {pid} is gone; cleaning up the leftover files
daemon.not_running: the daemon was not running anyway
daemon.pid_unreadable: the daemon is running ({sock}) but its pid file {pid_file} is unreadable; stop the process by hand
daemon.spawn_hint: to see why: run `browse daemon run --socket <path>` in the foreground
daemon.stop_timeout: sent SIGTERM but the daemon (pid {pid}) did not exit within {seconds}s
help:
browse — drive a browser extension from the command line

Usage
  browse <module> <action> [positional...] [--param value...]
  browse run [--concurrency N] [--no-fail-fast] '<command>'... | browse run -
  browse daemon start | stop | status
  browse stop                                       abort in-flight commands, keep the daemon
  browse install | uninstall                        install / remove (you still load the extension by hand once)

Get going
  browse install                                    first run: build + register + walk you through loading it
  browse browsingContext getTree --table            is the browser connected, which tabs are open
  browse browsingContext navigate https://example.com
  browse page snapshot --table                      list what is clickable / fillable on this page
  browse input type 'css=input[name=user]' 'myname'
  browse input click 'text=Sign in'
  browse script evaluate 'document.title'
  browse storage getCookies --domain example.com
  browse network subscribe --match-url '*/api/*' --duration 30s > api.jsonl
  browse run 'browsingContext.navigate https://a.com' 'browsingContext.navigate https://b.com'

Options (the CLI's own; every other --xxx is sent to the browser as a command param)
  --table            print the result as a table (stdout is plain JSON by default, pipe to jq)
  --socket PATH      which daemon socket file to use
  --concurrency N    run's concurrency cap, default 4
  --no-fail-fast     run keeps going after a failure, overall exit code 0
  --duration 30s     how long network subscribe listens; one JSON event per line
  --confirm-mode M   tighten the confirmation policy for this one command: silent / per_domain / always
                     tightening only; loosening must go in the config file and is refused here
  --lang L           language for this run: zh_CN / en
                     priority: --lang > lang in browse.yaml > LC_ALL/LANG/LANGUAGE > zh_CN
  --debug / --no-say repo-wide switches

Writing params
  --param names go kebab -> camel to become the wire key: --match-url is matchUrl
  values are parsed as JSON first, else kept as a string: --index 3 is a number, --domain a.com is a string
  to force a numeric-looking string, keep the JSON quotes: --text '"123"'
  four locator prefixes: css= / text= / xpath= / js=; no prefix means css=
  which tab: --context <id> > --match-url '<glob>' > the active tab

Confirmation (risky actions such as reading cookies or running JS)
  the policy is confirm_mode in ~/.config/lazygophers/scripts/browse.yaml:
  silent runs straight away (default) / per_domain asks once per domain / always asks every time
  when asked, the browser opens a small window and waits up to 60s; not clicking counts as a refusal (exit 4)
  domains in deny_domains are always refused, with no window at all

Exit codes
  0 ok   1 command failed   2 bad arguments   3 browser not connected   4 user refused

All commands
install.build_manual: build it by hand: cd {src} && npm install && npm run build
install.clipboard: (the path is on your clipboard — press Cmd+Shift+G in the file picker and paste)
install.connected: the extension is connected and the whole chain works. Try: browse browsingContext getTree --table
install.desc: register browse as the browser's native messaging host
install.err_browse_path_missing: --browse-path points at a file that does not exist: {path}
install.err_no_browse: browse is not on PATH and bin/browse is not in the repo either. Install it as a permanent command with `uv tool install git+https://github.com/lazygophers/scripts`, or point --browse-path at an absolute path that will not disappear
install.err_no_src: the extension source is not at {src}; pass --no-build to skip the build
install.interrupted: gave up waiting. Once loaded, check it yourself: {browse} browsingContext getTree --table
install.list.wrapper: wrapper (what the manifest's path points at): {path}
install.manual_load: the extension itself must be loaded by hand; see browser-extension/README.md
install.no_browser_detected: no browser detected ({plat}). A browser that has never been launched has no profile directory yet — name it with --browsers, picking from: {choices}
install.opt.browse_path: the absolute browse path written into the manifest
install.opt.browsers: comma separated; skip detection and name them, e.g. chrome,firefox
install.opt.extension_id: add one more Chromium extension ID (use this for the ID the Edge store issues)
install.opt.gecko_id: add one more Firefox extension ID (gecko.id)
install.opt.list: only print the detected browsers and locations, write nothing
install.opt.no_build: do not build the extension (by default npm run build runs when dist/ is missing)
install.opt.no_wait: return without waiting for the extension to connect (default waits 120s)
install.step2: 2. turn on Developer mode, top right (leave it on from now on)
install.step3: 3. click Load unpacked and pick this directory:
install.step_intro: One step left, and only you can click it — Chrome lets no program install an extension for the user:
install.timeout: timed out: the extension has not connected. Check, in order:
install.timeout1: 1. is the extension listed at chrome://extensions, and is it enabled
install.timeout2: 2. is the extension ID {ext_id} (if not, the manifest's key was changed)
install.timeout3: 3. click the service worker link on the extension card and read the console
install.verify_yourself: check it yourself once loaded: {browse} browsingContext getTree --table
install.waiting: waiting for you to load it… (up to {seconds}s, Ctrl-C to stop waiting)
run.cancelled: submitted to the browser, then cancelled by fail-fast; outcome unknown
run.skipped: an earlier command failed, so this one was never submitted
stop.done: aborted {count} in-flight command(s); the daemon is still running: {sock}
stop.no_daemon: the daemon is not running ({sock}), so nothing is in flight
usage.daemon_action: daemon only has start / stop / status: {action}
usage.duration_only_subscribe: --duration only means something for `browse network subscribe`
usage.item_has_cli_flags: `run` command strings cannot carry CLI options {opts}: {line}
usage.no_self_path: cannot find browse's own executable at {path}, so the daemon cannot be started
usage.no_such_command: no such command: {module} {action} (`browse --help` lists them all)
usage.run_needs_item: `run` needs at least one command string, or use `browse run -` to read stdin
usage.too_many_positional: {method} takes at most {count} positional argument(s); extra: {extra}
